passage: In Samir's kasba, the school bus drops everyone at the chowk, and most boys stay for tea and noise at the stall. Samir waves and walks home, climbs to the roof and lies on the charpai under the neem until the light changes. His cousin Ganga calls him "the professor" because he answers slowly and seems above the chatter. On Thursday their group presented a model of the canal system, and afterwards Samir was so tired he barely spoke at dinner. But when Ganga's bicycle chain broke on the way back from the fair, it was Samir who walked the whole four kilometres beside her, talking the entire way about why rivers bend.

qa.q: Where does Samir lie after school?
qa.a: He lies on the charpai under the neem on the roof.

qa.q: How did Samir feel after the presentation, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt drained by presenting with the group, so tired that he barely spoke at dinner.

qa.q: What choice did Samir make when Ganga's chain broke, and what did it show?
qa.a: He walked four kilometres beside her, talking the whole way, which showed his loyalty and how much he thinks about.

qa.q: How might Ganga see Samir after that walk?
qa.a: She may realise his slow answers are not snobbishness; he is a loyal cousin with plenty to say one-to-one.

grounding: A small-town teenager recharges alone after school, is drained by a group presentation and is mistaken for aloof, but is deep and loyal.

passage: Soo-ah's rule after school is simple: shoes off, door shut, headphones on, forty minutes with nothing. Her mother, in their Toronto apartment, has learned to leave the rice cooker on and knock later. In the group project on city parks, Astrid did most of the talking and told a friend that Soo-ah seemed "a bit cold". Soo-ah heard about it and said nothing for two days. On presentation day she spoke for her three minutes, clear and careful, then sat pale and still for the rest of the period. That night Astrid got a long message: a map Soo-ah had drawn of every park bench where old people sat alone, and an idea for the final slide. Astrid read it twice.

qa.q: What does Soo-ah do for forty minutes after school?
qa.a: Shoes off, door shut, headphones on, forty minutes with nothing.

qa.q: What does Soo-ah sitting pale and still after her three minutes suggest?
qa.a: It suggests speaking to the group drained her, even though she did it clearly.

qa.q: What choice did Soo-ah make after hearing the "cold" remark?
qa.a: She took two days, then sent Astrid a careful map and an idea, answering with her best work instead of an argument.

qa.q: How might Astrid see Soo-ah after reading the message twice?
qa.a: Astrid may realise "cold" was wrong; the quiet teammate had been thinking deeply all along.

grounding: A teenager recharges alone after school and is tired by presenting, is called cold by a teammate, and shows deep thought in writing.

passage:
Monday
Group presentation today. Five minutes of talking and I felt like I'd run a marathon. Payal did the intro, I did the data slides. Afterwards everyone went to the canteen and I came straight home and lay on my bed under the fan for an hour. Ammi knocked twice. 'Are you upset? You never talk any more.' I'm not upset. I'm just empty after people. And Sehar told someone I'm 'too proud to talk'. That stung. I'm not proud. I think before I speak, and by the time I've thought, the conversation has moved on. Payal texted at eight: 'You were great. Chai tomorrow, just us?' That's why she's my best friend. She never needs me to be loud.
Rehana

qa.q: What did Rehana do in the group presentation?
qa.a: The data slides.

qa.q: How did Rehana feel on hearing about the 'too proud to talk' comment?
qa.a: Rehana felt stung and misunderstood, not proud at all, just someone who thinks before speaking.

qa.q: How could Rehana answer Ammi's worry?
qa.a: By explaining that time alone after school is how Rehana recharges, not a sign of being upset, and maybe suggesting a quiet chat later.

qa.q: Why does Payal's text matter so much to Rehana?
qa.a: Payal praises Rehana and offers chai for just the two of them, a loyal friend who never needs Rehana to be loud.

grounding: Shows a teenager who is drained by a group presentation, recharges alone, is mistaken for proud, and has a deep, loyal friendship.

passage:
Vandana: party at Sid's tonight, u coming?
Nikita: can't today
Vandana: u said that last time
Vandana: ppl think ur a snob btw
Nikita: oh
Nikita: i'm not. after school i just need to be alone for a bit, it's like charging
Vandana: charging from what, school??
Nikita: yeah honestly. 6 hours of noise. and today was the group presentation
Vandana: u were good in it tho
Nikita: thanks. took me 3 days to plan what to say
Vandana: wait really
Nikita: i think a lot before i talk. by the time i know what to say at parties everyone's moved on
Vandana: that's actually kind of interesting
Nikita: movie sunday? just u and me. i'll actually talk 🙂
Vandana: deal

qa.q: Where was the party?
qa.a: At Sid's.

qa.q: What might Nikita have felt reading 'ppl think ur a snob'?
qa.a: Nikita probably felt hurt and misunderstood, replying only 'oh' before explaining.

qa.q: What did Nikita do that helped Vandana understand?
qa.a: Nikita explained honestly about needing time alone to recharge and offered a one-to-one movie, showing it isn't coldness.

qa.q: How does Vandana's view of Nikita change during the chat?
qa.a: Vandana starts out annoyed, repeating the 'snob' idea, then finds Nikita's way of thinking interesting and agrees to Sunday.

grounding: Shows a teenager who needs time alone after school, thinks before speaking, finds presentations tiring, and is mistaken for a snob by a friend.

passage: Every day after school in their village near Bikaner, Neelam climbed to the roof with her notebook and stayed there till the cows came home. Her brother Nilesh called her 'the queen upstairs'. At the youth meeting in the panchayat hall that week, everyone argued loudly about the new water tank. Neelam sat silent for an hour. Then, near the end, she raised her hand. 'If the tank goes by the temple, the families in the lower basti will walk twice as far. Can it go in between?' The hall went quiet. The sarpanch wrote it down. Walking home, Nilesh kicked a stone. 'Where did that come from?' 'From the roof,' she said. 'I think better up there.' That evening her friend Kiran came with two cups of chai, and they sat on the roof together, hardly talking, the way they had since Class 2.

qa.q: What did Neelam suggest about the water tank?
qa.a: That it go in between, so the families in the lower basti wouldn't walk twice as far.

qa.q: How might Neelam have felt sitting silent for an hour at the meeting?
qa.a: She was probably calm and absorbed, thinking carefully before speaking, rather than bored or aloof.

qa.q: What could Nilesh learn from the meeting?
qa.a: That Neelam's time alone on the roof is where her ideas form, so calling her 'the queen upstairs' misreads her.

qa.q: How might Kiran see Neelam?
qa.a: Kiran, a friend since Class 2, sees a loyal, easy companion to share quiet chai with, not someone aloof.

grounding: Shows a teenager who recharges alone, thinks before speaking and is mistaken for aloof, yet offers a deep idea and keeps a long, loyal friendship.

passage: In Prague, Tomas, fifteen, came home from school every day, said "Ahoj" to his mother and shut his door. Guitar, headphones, silence. In class he spoke rarely, thinking long before answering, and group presentations left him wiped out for the evening. Some classmates called him arrogant. Fatima, his friend since they were eight, knew better. On Saturday he played her a song he'd written, slow and careful, about her grandmother's hospital stay last winter. She hadn't known he'd noticed how scared she'd been. Fatima wiped her eyes. "You remember everything." Tomas shrugged, embarrassed. "I just listen." On Monday, when a boy mocked her accent, Tomas was the one who quietly stood beside her.

qa.q: What did Tomas's song describe?
qa.a: Fatima's grandmother's hospital stay last winter.

qa.q: How does Tomas feel after group presentations?
qa.a: He feels tired and wiped out for the evening, needing quiet to recharge.

qa.q: What does the song show that classmates miss about Tomas?
qa.a: It shows his deep thoughtfulness and loyalty, which classmates mistake for arrogance.

qa.q: How did Fatima feel when she heard the song?
qa.a: She felt moved and understood, wiping her eyes because Tomas had noticed her fear.

grounding: Shows a teenager who recharges alone, thinks before speaking and tires of group work, mistaken for aloof but deep-thinking and loyal to a friend.
